correctness.rationale: PASS: Binary column-prefix constraints give ≤i−1 negatives and norm²≤m² for every row; pairing negative entries in the cross inner product yields the universal 2m(2m−1) squared Frobenius bound. Equality forces row sums one and full negative counts, disjoint positive supports, and staggered alternating bottom-row positives on 2m columns; backward interlacing proves exactly one unordered pair per 2m-column choice. Explicit diamond matrices attain the bound; transpose covers m>n; strict convexity excludes nonvertex endpoints. Independently generated every PASM for (1,1),(1,3),(2,3..6),(3,5..6): computed exact diameters and saturation counts 1,5,15,1. This is bounded corroboration, not an all-dimension certificate.
